# Pixel Tune **Reversible performance, thermal and battery tuning for the Google Pixel 8a** ![Version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/MildaHribal/pixel_tune?style=flat-square) ![Device](https://img.shields.io/badge/device-Pixel%208a%20(akita)-4285F4?style=flat-square&logo=google&logoColor=white) ![KernelSU](https://img.shields.io/badge/root-KernelSU--Next-2E7D32?style=flat-square) ![Shell](https://img.shields.io/badge/POSIX%20sh-4EAA25?style=flat-square&logo=gnubash&logoColor=white) ![WebUI](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebUI-HTML%20%2F%20JS-E34F26?style=flat-square&logo=html5&logoColor=white)
> [!WARNING] > Built and measured **only for the Pixel 8a (Tensor G3)**. The sysfs paths, frequency tables and thermal values are SoC-specific. Do not install it on any other device. ## About A KernelSU module that puts the Pixel 8a's hidden tuning levers (uclamp, the `sched_pixel` governor, the Mali GPU, the memory bus, MGLRU, charge cap) behind one CLI and a WebUI. It exists because the phone throttles hard: under sustained load the big cores drop to ~38-40 % of their maximum at only 58 °C, and take ~84 s to recover. The profiles therefore trim the thermal peak instead of chasing benchmark numbers. ## Features - **Profiles, switched by hand**: `balanced` (default), `powersave`, `performance`, `game`, `night`, `pogo`. No background daemon decides for you. - **WebUI** in the KernelSU manager: live CPU/GPU/temperature/battery overview, profile tiles, charge-limit slider, per-app rules, tweaks, sleep settings. - **Tweak registry**: kernel/system knobs, each with a description, risk level and stock value. - **Per-app rules**: Android Game Mode, refresh rate and a profile overlay per package. - **Sleep helper** (`pxtune doze`): releases foreign wake locks so the phone can actually suspend. - **Charge cap**, display resolution/DPI presets with a 60 s auto-revert safeguard, optional metrics sampling. ## Safety - Everything is **reversible**: stock values are snapshotted on first run and `pxtune revert` restores them. - Writes nothing to `/system` or `/vendor`, mounts no overlay, SELinux stays **Enforcing**. - **Bootloop protection**: the module disables itself after repeated failed boots. - Emergency off switch: create `/data/adb/pixel_tune/DISABLE`, or boot into KernelSU safe mode. ## Requirements - Google Pixel 8a, Android 16 (tested on kernel `6.1.145-android14-11`) - Root with **KernelSU-Next** (the tested setup; the WebUI needs a manager with module WebUI support) ## Installation 1. Download `pixel_tune-vX.Y.Z.zip` from [**Releases**](https://github.com/MildaHribal/pixel_tune/releases/latest). 2. KernelSU manager → **Modules** → **Install from storage** → pick the ZIP. 3. Reboot. The profile is applied ~20 s after boot, once the system is up. 4. Check that everything is in place: ```sh su -c 'pxtune selftest' ``` To uninstall, remove it in the manager and reboot; `uninstall.sh` reverts the runtime values. Your profiles and the stock backup in `/data/adb/pixel_tune/` are kept. ## Usage Open the WebUI from the manager (**Modules → Pixel Tune → WebUI**), or use the CLI as root: ```sh pxtune status # profile, temperatures, frequencies, battery pxtune profile powersave # switch profile pxtune charge 80 # stop charging at 80 % pxtune tweak list # browse the tweak registry pxtune app list # per-app rules pxtune doze on # enable the sleep helper pxtune revert # restore everything to stock pxtune log # last 50 log lines ``` ## Project structure ``` bin/ pxtune CLI and its helpers (tweaks, per-app, metrics, doze) profiles/ shipped profiles (KEY=VALUE, parsed, never sourced) tweaks/ the tweak registry apps/ example per-app rules webroot/ the WebUI *.sh KernelSU lifecycle scripts (install, boot, uninstall) ``` ## Documentation The full guide covers how every profile value was derived, the complete CLI and profile-key reference, the four levels of emergency shutdown, troubleshooting and a full manual revert: **[docs/GUIDE.md](docs/GUIDE.md)**. The internal contract is in [SPEC.md](SPEC.md).

Pixel Tune

Reversible performance, thermal and battery tuning for the Google Pixel 8a

!Version

!Device-4285F4?style=flat-square&logo=google&logoColor=white)

!KernelSU

!Shell

!WebUI

> [!WARNING]

> Built and measured only for the Pixel 8a (Tensor G3). The sysfs paths, frequency tables and thermal values are SoC-specific. Do not install it on any other device.

About

A KernelSU module that puts the Pixel 8a's hidden tuning levers (uclamp, the sched_pixel governor, the Mali GPU, the memory bus, MGLRU, charge cap) behind one CLI and a WebUI. It exists because the phone throttles hard: under sustained load the big cores drop to ~38-40 % of their maximum at only 58 °C, and take ~84 s to recover. The profiles therefore trim the thermal peak instead of chasing benchmark numbers.

Features

  • **Profiles, switched by hand**: `balanced` (default), `powersave`, `performance`, `game`, `night`, `pogo`. No background daemon decides for you.
  • **WebUI** in the KernelSU manager: live CPU/GPU/temperature/battery overview, profile tiles, charge-limit slider, per-app rules, tweaks, sleep settings.
  • **Tweak registry**: kernel/system knobs, each with a description, risk level and stock value.
  • **Per-app rules**: Android Game Mode, refresh rate and a profile overlay per package.
  • **Sleep helper** (`pxtune doze`): releases foreign wake locks so the phone can actually suspend.
  • **Charge cap**, display resolution/DPI presets with a 60 s auto-revert safeguard, optional metrics sampling.

    • Safety

  • Everything is **reversible**: stock values are snapshotted on first run and `pxtune revert` restores them.
  • Writes nothing to `/system` or `/vendor`, mounts no overlay, SELinux stays **Enforcing**.
  • **Bootloop protection**: the module disables itself after repeated failed boots.
  • Emergency off switch: create `/data/adb/pixel_tune/DISABLE`, or boot into KernelSU safe mode.

    • Requirements

  • Google Pixel 8a, Android 16 (tested on kernel `6.1.145-android14-11`)
  • Root with **KernelSU-Next** (the tested setup; the WebUI needs a manager with module WebUI support)

    • Installation

  • Download `pixel_tune-vX.Y.Z.zip` from [**Releases**](https://github.com/MildaHribal/pixel_tune/releases/latest).
  • KernelSU manager → **Modules** → **Install from storage** → pick the ZIP.
  • Reboot. The profile is applied ~20 s after boot, once the system is up.
  • Check that everything is in place:
    • su -c 'pxtune selftest'

    To uninstall, remove it in the manager and reboot; uninstall.sh reverts the runtime values. Your profiles and the stock backup in /data/adb/pixel_tune/ are kept.

    Usage

    Open the WebUI from the manager (Modules → Pixel Tune → WebUI), or use the CLI as root:

    pxtune status               # profile, temperatures, frequencies, battery
pxtune profile powersave    # switch profile
pxtune charge 80            # stop charging at 80 %
pxtune tweak list           # browse the tweak registry
pxtune app list             # per-app rules
pxtune doze on              # enable the sleep helper
pxtune revert               # restore everything to stock
pxtune log                  # last 50 log lines

    Project structure

    bin/          pxtune CLI and its helpers (tweaks, per-app, metrics, doze)
profiles/     shipped profiles (KEY=VALUE, parsed, never sourced)
tweaks/       the tweak registry
apps/         example per-app rules
webroot/      the WebUI
*.sh          KernelSU lifecycle scripts (install, boot, uninstall)

    Documentation

    The full guide covers how every profile value was derived, the complete CLI and profile-key reference, the four levels of emergency shutdown, troubleshooting and a full manual revert: docs/GUIDE.md. The internal contract is in SPEC.md.
